doc.title: Mark Soskin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 17, 2021

title: Overdubs versus live recording
summary: His record dates are played live with everyone together rather than overdubbed.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Have you ever had a recording date where you were accompanying a singer or a soloist who was not even there? In other words you’re laying down accompaniment for somebody to put something over it later?
My question is I wonder if you’ve ever been in that situation like you’re comping but you don’t know what’s going to go over the top of this.
So it’s kind of an odd feeling that I can’t respond to the soloist or the singer because they’re going to do this later.
Yeah. I mean usually when I do a record date it’s really not so much about that.
It’s not so much about overdubbing. It’s live. We’re all playing live and I know what to do.
